en.headline: West Kowloon eyes 2027/28 as turning point towards operating returns
en.dek: Board chairman Bernard Chan told lawmakers the cultural district recorded its highest operating revenue yet and expects major facilities to shift the focus from cash flow to self-sustaining income.
body: The West Kowloon Cultural District Authority told the Legislative Council's Panel on Home Affairs, Culture and Sports on Monday that 2027/28 would mark a watershed, with the district entering a new phase and moving towards an operating harvest period.

Board chairman Bernard Chan said operating revenue reached HK$768 million in 2025/26, the highest since the authority was established and a year-on-year increase of nearly 20 per cent. He noted that deficits are normal for cultural facilities, but the district has been building the capacity to generate income, with ticketing and sponsorship revenue each rising more than 30 per cent and retail income more than doubling.

Chan said the West Kowloon Performing Arts Centre, Artist Square Towers and an extension of the harbourfront promenade are due for completion around that time. He added that the challenge would then shift from cash-flow concerns to leveraging the district's hardware and software advantages to create revenue without further government funding, while continuing to accelerate commercial projects to broaden income sources.

zh.headline: 西九文化區2027/28年度邁向營運收成期
zh.dek: 管理局董事局主席陳智思向立法會議員表示，西九上年度營運收入創新高，預期隨主要設施落成，重點將由現金流轉為自我持續收入。
body: 西九文化區管理局星期一向立法會民政及文化體育事務委員會匯報，指2027/28年度將是分水嶺，文化區發展將進入新階段，逐步邁向營運收成期。
董事局主席陳智思表示，2025/26年度營運收入達7.68億元，是管理局成立以來最高，按年升近兩成。他指出文化設施出現赤字屬正常，但西九已逐步建立創造收入能力，門票及贊助收入各增逾三成，零售收入更按年倍增。
陳智思說，西九演藝中心、藝術廣場大樓及海濱長廊延展部分預計於該時期相繼落成。屆時挑戰不再是現金流，而是在毋需政府注資下，善用硬件及軟件優勢創造收入，同時加快商業發展項目以拓寬收入來源。
